lead.headline: US State Department formally integrates Bitcoin policy and defense-tech contractors under diplomatic umbrella
lead.tldr: Today's throughline is the widening gap between two regulatory regimes: Washington is actively recruiting crypto-adjacent firms into national-security infrastructure, while Brussels and Bangkok escalate enforcement against exchanges. The market is being asked to price sovereign adoption and sovereign crackdown simultaneously.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today's brief tracks how governments are resolving their ambivalence toward crypto not by choosing one posture but by running contradictory ones in parallel, with material consequences for where capital can safely land.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute, Palantir and Anduril join US State Department's Freedom Tech Excellence Program
top_signals.summary: The Bitcoin Policy Institute has partnered with Palantir and Anduril as part of the U.S. State Department's Freedom Tech Excellence Program. This represents a significant integration of Bitcoin-focused policy and advanced technology firms within U.S. diplomatic and governmental frameworks.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The State Department's inclusion of Bitcoin Policy Institute alongside Palantir and Anduril signals that Bitcoin is being underwritten as strategic infrastructure rather than tolerated as speculative asset class, which reprices regulatory risk for US-facing infrastructure plays.

top_signals.title: EU authorities include HTX exchange in Russian sanctions36m, EU authorities include HTX exchange in Russian sanctionsThe exchange, already sanctioned by the UK, is now on a list of 18 entities “providing crypto-assets services or payment services“ in defiance of the EU’s measures against Russia.
top_signals.summary: EU authorities have added the HTX cryptocurrency exchange to a sanctions list for allegedly providing services that bypass measures against Russia. HTX is one of 18 entities identified as providing crypto-asset or payment services in defiance of EU regulations.
top_signals.why_it_matters: HTX's addition to the EU sanctions list demonstrates that exchange compliance programs are now being stress-tested against geopolitical enforcement rather than mere AML box-checking, raising the cost of capital for offshore venues serving gray-market demand.

top_signals.title: World Foundation raises $52.5M in Pantera-led funding to expand World ID infrastructure16m
top_signals.summary: World Foundation has secured $52.5 million in a funding round led by Pantera Capital. The capital will be used to further expand and develop the World ID infrastructure.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Pantera's lead in World Foundation's $52.5M round indicates that despite consumer-facing skepticism, institutional capital continues to underwrite identity infrastructure at the protocol layer, betting that proof-of-personhood becomes extractable value rather than public good.

top_signals.title: Thailand SEC Files Complaint Against Bitkub Over 2021 Hack Reporting
top_signals.summary: The Thailand SEC has filed a complaint against Bitkub and two former directors regarding false disclosures following a 2021 cyberattack. The hack in question resulted in losses totaling approximately $50 million.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Thailand SEC's complaint against Bitkub for 2021 hack disclosures reveals that historical incident response is becoming fair game for retroactive enforcement, extending statute-of-limitations risk for exchanges with legacy compliance gaps.

top_signals.title: Arthur Hayes, BitMEX co-founders face fraud claims over alleged 'Insider Trading Desk' as exchange winds down
top_signals.summary: BitMEX co-founders Arthur Hayes, Samuel Reed, and Benjamin Delo are facing a proposed class action lawsuit. The claims allege the existence of an 'insider trading desk' and the intentional freezing of servers to manipulate outcomes.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The BitMEX insider trading desk allegations resurfacing during wind-down proceedings show that founder liability does not terminate with operational exit, complicating M&A underwriting for exchange assets with opaque trading histories.

Mirae Asset has completed the acquisition of Korbit, officially becoming the largest shareholder of the South Korean cryptocurrency exchange. This move signals a significant expansion of a major traditional financial institution into the digital asset market.

on_the_radar.title: Samsung Wallet to Add Stablecoin Support
on_the_radar.summary: Samsung is expanding the capabilities of Samsung Wallet by adding support for stablecoins. This move follows the previous integration of cryptocurrency purchasing features via Coinbase.

on_the_radar.title: Hopes for key crypto bill fade amid delays, Trump ethics controversy
on_the_radar.summary: The CLARITY Act, a key piece of cryptocurrency legislation, is facing significant delays and may not pass due to mid-term political pressures. The bill's progress is further complicated by ethics controversies surrounding Donald Trump.

on_the_radar.title: BitMEX hit with 623 BTC lawsuit on day it announces shutdown 7m, BitMEX hit with 623 BTC lawsuit on day it announces shutdown The proposed class action alleges BitMEX used privileged trading access and server freezes to profit from forced liquidations.
on_the_radar.summary: BitMEX is facing a class action lawsuit seeking 623 BTC over allegations of market manipulation and unfair trading practices. The lawsuit claims the exchange used privileged access and server freezes to profit from forced user liquidations.

on_the_radar.title: Kakao, Circle Explore Won Stablecoin Payment Infrastructure
on_the_radar.summary: Kakao, Kakao Pay, and Kakao Bank are partnering with Circle to explore stablecoin-based payments, remittances, and tokenized finance. This initiative aligns with South Korea's broader efforts to establish a comprehensive digital asset regulatory framework.

on_the_radar.title: Wise plans to resubmit national trust bank application under GENIUS Act framework
on_the_radar.summary: Wise is planning to resubmit its application for a national trust bank charter utilizing the GENIUS Act framework. This move follows the OCC's trend of granting conditional approval to stablecoin-focused entities.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto Advocacy Groups Support CLARITY Passage as Ethics Rules Face Pushback
on_the_radar.summary: Three crypto industry advocacy groups are urging the US Senate to consider the CLARITY Act despite potential roadblocks regarding proposed ethics rules. The effort aims to push the bill forward to establish clearer regulatory frameworks for the industry.

on_the_radar.title: Weekly Top Stories: Clarity Act Falls to 30% Odds
on_the_radar.summary: The Clarity Act's probability of passing has dropped to 30%. Additionally, a new Quantum Security Consortium for Bitcoin has launched, and an AI model reportedly compromised Hugging Face.

on_the_radar.summary: Odos Protocol has announced its decision to shut down operations. Users have been instructed to withdraw their assets from the platform by July 30.

linkedin_post:
The State Department just put Bitcoin Policy Institute in the same program as Anduril and Palantir. Not a side event. The same diplomatic infrastructure.

This is not crypto lobbying. This is crypto being absorbed into national-security procurement logic. The Freedom Tech Excellence Program frames Bitcoin as censorship-resistant infrastructure for adversarial environments—meaning the US government now underwrites it explicitly for use cases that traditional finance cannot serve.

We have spent years pricing regulatory risk as binary: friendly or hostile. Washington is running a third option. Recruit the technology, regulate the retail speculation separately. The BPI-Anduril-Palantir grouping tells us which verticals get the green light.

Meanwhile HTX hits EU sanctions lists and Thailand's SEC retroactively pursues Bitkub for a 2021 hack. The divergence is the signal. Capital will reprice jurisdictional premium faster than founders can relocate.

Pantera putting $52.5M into World Foundation's identity infrastructure reads correctly against this backdrop. Proof-of-personhood becomes more valuable when sovereigns are actively sorting who gets to participate in which financial system.

What we are watching: whether any US legislator challenges State's framing of Bitcoin as diplomatic tool, or whether this institutionalizes without opposition. That vote, or its absence, reprices the entire US infrastructure stack.
